Vani Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vani, Georgia

Not demolished. Vani, an ancient settlement in Georgia's Imereti region dating to the 6th century BCE, saw Jewish settlement from the late 18th century, likely connected to nearby Kutaisi and Kulashi's established communities. This cemetery, on the Chishura River near the town's synagogue (built 1911), holds burials documented from 1885 through the last recorded burial in 1989. The synagogue, a 180-square-meter stone-and-brick building, drew about 160 attendees on holidays and 60 regularly by the mid-20th century. Notable native son Shabtai Tsur, born in Vani in 1951, served twice as Israel's ambassador to Georgia; a main street in Vani now bears his name.
